title.zh: 卷318 列傳一百五 阿桂 阿迪斯 阿必达
title.en: Volume 318 Biographies 105: A Gui, A Di Si, A Bi Da
title.raw: 卷318 列傳一百五 阿桂 阿迪斯 阿必达

sentences.zh: 阿桂，字廣庭，章佳氏。

translations.literal: A Gui, style name Guangting, of the Zhangjia clan.
translations.idiomatic: A Gui, whose style name was Guangting, belonged to the Zhangjia clan.

sentences.zh: 初為滿洲正藍旗人，以阿桂平回部駐伊犁治事有勞，改隸正白旗。

translations.literal: At first he was a Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner; because A Gui pacified the Muslim regions and had merit governing affairs while stationed at Yili, he was transferred to the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was originally registered in the Manchu Plain Blue Banner; after he helped pacify the Muslim west and distinguished himself administering Yili, he was reassigned to the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 父大學士阿克敦，自有傳。

translations.literal: His father was the Grand Secretary Akedun, who has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Grand Secretary Akedun, treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 阿桂，乾隆三年舉人。

translations.literal: A Gui became a provincial graduate in the third year of Qianlong.
translations.idiomatic: A Gui passed the provincial examination in the third year of the Qianlong reign.

sentences.zh: 初以父廕授大理寺丞，累遷吏部員外郎，充軍機處章京。

translations.literal: At first, through his father's privilege of office, he was appointed vice director of the Court of Judicial Review; he was promoted through several posts to vice director in the Ministry of Personnel and served as a clerk in the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered service by hereditary privilege as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, then rose through several posts to vice director in the Ministry of Personnel and served as a Grand Council clerk.

sentences.zh: 十三年，從兵部尚書班第參金川軍事。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he followed the Minister of War Ban Di to take part in the Jinchuan campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he accompanied Minister of War Ban Di on the Jinchuan campaign.

sentences.zh: 訥親、張​​廣泗以無功被罪，岳鍾琪劾阿桂結張廣泗蔽訥親，逮問。

translations.literal: Neqin and Zhang Guangsi were punished for achieving no results; Yue Zhongqi impeached A Gui for colluding with Zhang Guangsi to shield Neqin, and he was arrested for inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: When Neqin and Zhang Guangsi were punished for their failures, Yue Zhongqi accused A Gui of colluding with Zhang Guangsi to cover for Neqin, and he was taken into custody for investigation.

sentences.zh: 十四年，上以阿克敦年老，無次子，治事勤勉；

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the emperor considered that Akedun was elderly, had no second son, and was diligent in office;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year the emperor noted that Akedun was old, had no other son, and had served diligently;

sentences.zh: 阿桂罪與貽誤軍事不同，特旨宥之。

translations.literal: A Gui's offense was not the same as causing military failure, and he was specially pardoned by imperial decree.
translations.idiomatic: A Gui's fault was not of the sort that had derailed the campaign, and the emperor specially pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 尋复官，擢江西按察使，召補內閣侍讀學士。

translations.literal: Soon afterward his office was restored; he was promoted to Jiangxi surveillance commissioner and summoned to fill the post of associate reader in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored to office, promoted to surveillance commissioner of Jiangxi, and recalled to serve as associate reader in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十年，擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was promoted to Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was promoted to Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 時方徵準噶爾，命阿桂赴烏里雅蘇台督台站。

translations.literal: At that time the Dzungar campaign was under way, and A Gui was ordered to go to Uliassutai to supervise courier stations.
translations.idiomatic: While the campaign against the Dzungars was in progress, he was sent to Uliassutai to oversee the courier stations.

sentences.zh: 逾年，父喪還京。

translations.literal: After more than a year, upon his father's death he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: A year later, after his father's death, he returned to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 旋復遣赴軍，授參贊大臣，命駐科布多，授鑲紅旗蒙古副都統。

translations.literal: Soon he was again dispatched to the army, appointed assisting commander, ordered to garrison Khobdo, and given the post of Mongol vice commander-in-chief of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent back to the front as assisting commander, stationed at Khobdo, and appointed Mongol vice commander-in-chief of the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 二十二年秋，授工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the twenty-second year he was appointed vice minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn of the twenty-second year he was appointed vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 輝特頭人舍楞約降，唐喀祿以兵往會，為所襲，阿桂率兵策應，上嘉之，賜花翎。

translations.literal: The Khoit chief Sereng offered to surrender; Tang Kalu went with troops to meet him and was ambushed; A Gui led troops in support, and the emperor commended him and bestowed peacock feathers.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khoit chief Sereng offered to submit, Tang Kalu marched out to receive him and was ambushed; A Gui brought up reinforcements, and the emperor praised him and awarded peacock feathers.

sentences.zh: 上命阿桂與策布登扎布合軍擊舍楞，毋使逃入俄羅斯。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered A Gui and Tsebudengjab to join forces and attack Sereng, not allowing him to escape into Russia.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered A Gui and Tsebudengjab to combine forces against Sereng and keep him from fleeing into Russia.

sentences.zh: 阿桂言：「得降賊，謂舍楞將逃土爾扈特；

translations.literal: A Gui said: "Among the surrendered bandits it is said that Sereng will flee to the Torghuts;
translations.idiomatic: A Gui reported: "From the surrendered rebels we hear that Sereng intends to flee to the Torghuts;

sentences.zh: 或不達，且復回準噶爾。

translations.literal: or if he does not reach them, he may yet return to Dzungaria.
translations.idiomatic: and if he cannot reach them, he may yet circle back into Dzungaria.

sentences.zh: 邀之中路，可擒獻。」

translations.literal: if we intercept him midway, we can capture him and present him."
translations.idiomatic: If we cut him off along the route, we can take him alive and present him as a captive."

sentences.zh: 上責其觀望，召還京。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked him for holding back, and summoned him back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accused him of hesitation, and recalled him to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 是年準部平，復命赴西路，與副將軍富德追捕餘賊。

translations.literal: That year the Dzungar region was pacified, and he was again ordered to the western route to pursue remaining bandits with the deputy commander Fude.
translations.idiomatic: That year, with Dzungaria pacified, he was again sent west with Deputy Commander Fude to hunt down the remaining rebels.

sentences.zh: 霍集占叛，二十四年，命赴霍斯庫魯克從富德進討。

translations.literal: Hojijan rebelled; in the twenty-fourth year A Gui was ordered to Hoskurluk to follow Fude in the advance against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hojijan rose in revolt, in the twenty-fourth year he was ordered to Hoskurluk to join Fude's advance.

sentences.zh: 八月，逐賊至阿勒楚爾，又至伊西洱庫爾淖爾，回眾降。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he pursued the rebels to Altishahr and then to Lake Yashilkul; the Muslim populace submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he drove the rebels to Altishahr and then to Lake Yashilkul, where the Muslim communities submitted.

sentences.zh: 霍集占走拔達克山。

translations.literal: Hojijan fled to Badakhshan.
translations.idiomatic: Hojijan fled into Badakhshan.

sentences.zh: 是年回部平。

translations.literal: That year the Muslim regions were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Muslim west was brought under control.

sentences.zh: 上以阿克蘇新附，為回部要地，命阿桂駐軍綏撫。

translations.literal: The emperor considered that Aksu had newly submitted and was a key place in the Muslim regions, and ordered A Gui to garrison troops there to pacify and reassure the people.
translations.idiomatic: Because Aksu had only recently submitted and was a strategic point in the Muslim west, the emperor ordered A Gui to station troops there and pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，移駐伊犁。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he moved his garrison to Yili.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he transferred his headquarters to Yili.

sentences.zh: 阿桂上言伊犁屯田、阿克蘇調兵諸事。

translations.literal: A Gui memorialized on Yili garrison farming, troop transfers at Aksu, and related matters.
translations.idiomatic: A Gui submitted memorials on garrison farming at Yili, troop deployments from Aksu, and related measures.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其勇往，命專司耕作營造，務使軍士、回民皆樂於從事。

translations.literal: The emperor commended his boldness and ordered him to take charge of farming and construction, seeing to it that soldiers and Muslim subjects alike were willing to take part.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his energy and put him in charge of farming and construction, insisting that both soldiers and Muslim settlers take satisfaction in the work.

sentences.zh: 時西域初定，地方萬餘裡，伏莽尚眾，與俄羅斯鄰。

translations.literal: At that time the western regions had just been pacified; the territory extended more than ten thousand li, hidden malcontents were still numerous, and it bordered Russia.
translations.idiomatic: The western frontier had only just been secured: the territory stretched more than ten thousand li, armed bands still lurked in the hills, and the border lay against Russia.

sentences.zh: 上詔統兵諸大臣議，咸謂沙漠遼遠，牲畜凋耗，難駐守。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the commanders-in-chief to deliberate, and all said the deserts were vast and remote, livestock were depleted, and garrisons would be hard to maintain.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor convened the field commanders for discussion; they all argued that the deserts were too vast, livestock too scarce, and permanent garrisons impracticable.

sentences.zh: 阿桂疏言：「守邊以駐兵為先，駐兵​​以軍食為要。

translations.literal: A Gui memorialized: "To guard the frontier, stationing troops comes first; for stationed troops, military provisions are essential.
translations.idiomatic: A Gui argued in a memorial: "Frontier defense depends first on keeping troops in place, and keeping troops in place depends on food supplies.

sentences.zh: 伊犁河以南海努克等處，水土沃衍，宜屯田。

translations.literal: South of the Ili River, at Hanuke and other places, the soil and water are rich and suitable for garrison farming.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Ili River, around Hanuke and elsewhere, the land is fertile and well suited to garrison colonies.

sentences.zh: 請增遣回民嫺耕作者往屯；

translations.literal: I request that more Muslim subjects skilled in farming be sent to colonize;
translations.idiomatic: I ask that more Muslim farmers skilled at cultivation be sent to settle there;

sentences.zh: 增派官兵駐防，協同耕種；

translations.literal: that more officers and soldiers be assigned to garrison defense and farm together;
translations.idiomatic: that additional troops be posted to garrison the area and farm alongside them;

sentences.zh: 次第建置城邑；

translations.literal: that towns be built in stages;
translations.idiomatic: that towns be built up step by step;

sentences.zh: 預籌馬駝，置台站；

translations.literal: that horses and camels be provided in advance and courier stations established;
translations.idiomatic: that horses and camels be provisioned in advance and courier stations set up;

sentences.zh: 運沿邊米赴伊犁；

translations.literal: that grain from the border regions be transported to Yili;
translations.idiomatic: that grain from the border provinces be shipped to Yili;

sentences.zh: 簡各省流人嫺工藝者，發備任使。」

translations.literal: and that exiles from the provinces skilled in crafts be selected and dispatched for service as needed."
translations.idiomatic: and that exiled convicts from the provinces who are skilled in crafts be selected and assigned as required."

sentences.zh: 又奏定山川、土穀諸祀典，上用其議。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to fix the ritual codes for sacrifices to mountains, rivers, and the god of the soil and grain, and the emperor adopted his proposals.
translations.idiomatic: He also drew up the ritual regulations for sacrifices to mountains, rivers, and the god of soil and grain, which the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 阿桂造農器，督諸屯耕穫，歲大豐。

translations.literal: A Gui made farm implements, supervised the garrison colonies in plowing and harvest, and the year brought a great abundance.
translations.idiomatic: A Gui designed farm tools, oversaw the garrison farms through planting and harvest, and that year the yields were abundant.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，疏言：「伊犁牧群蕃息，請停內地購馬駝。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he memorialized: "The herds at Yili have multiplied; I request that purchases of horses and camels from the interior be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he reported: "The herds at Yili have flourished; I ask that the court stop buying horses and camels from the interior provinces.

sentences.zh: 增招葉爾羌、喀什噶爾、阿克蘇、烏什回民詣伊犁，廣屯田。」

translations.literal: Recruit more Muslim subjects from Yarkand, Kashgar, Aksu, and Ush to come to Yili and expand garrison farming."
translations.idiomatic: Recruit more Muslims from Yarkand, Kashgar, Aksu, and Ush to settle at Yili and expand the garrison farms.

sentences.zh: 皆稱旨。

translations.literal: All were deemed to accord with the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: All of these proposals met with the emperor's approval.

sentences.zh: 迭授內大臣、工部尚書、鑲藍旗漢軍都統，仍駐伊犁。

translations.literal: In succession he was appointed inner court minister, Minister of Works, and commander-in-chief of the Bordered Blue Banner Chinese forces, while still garrisoned at Yili.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively appointed inner court minister, Minister of Works, and commander-in-chief of the Bordered Blue Banner Chinese forces, while remaining stationed at Yili.

sentences.zh: 奏瑪納斯庫爾、喀喇烏蘇、晶河三地屯田，人授十五畝。

translations.literal: He memorialized on garrison farming at Manas, Kur, Karasu, and Jinghe, allotting fifteen mu per person.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed garrison colonies at Manas, Kur, Karasu, and Jinghe, with fifteen mu allotted to each settler.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，疏定約束章程，建綏定、安遠二城，兵居、民房次第立，一如內地，數千里行旅晏然，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he memorialized to fix regulations and codes of conduct, built the two cities of Suiding and Anyuan, and had barracks and civilian houses erected in order like those in the interior; travelers over thousands of li went in peace, and he was granted the hereditary office of commandant of cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he drew up governing regulations, founded the cities of Suiding and Anyuan, and had barracks and civilian quarters built up in the manner of the interior provinces; for thousands of li travelers passed in safety, and he was granted the hereditary rank of commandant of cavalry.

sentences.zh: 召還，賜紫禁城騎馬，命軍機處行走。

translations.literal: He was recalled, granted the privilege of riding a horse within the Forbidden City, and ordered to serve in the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was granted the rare privilege of riding a horse inside the Forbidden City and appointed to serve in the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 調正紅旗滿洲都統，加太子太保。

translations.literal: He was transferred to commander-in-chief of the Plain Red Banner Manchu forces and given the additional title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commander-in-chief of the Plain Red Banner Manchus and given the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，命署伊犁將軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was ordered to act as Ili general.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was appointed acting general of Yili.

sentences.zh: 尋調署四川總督。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to act as governor-general of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to serve as acting governor-general of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 時金川土司郎卡與綽斯甲布等九土司構釁，阿桂巡邊，盡得郎卡狡獪怙惡狀，並悉其山川形勢，入奏。

translations.literal: At that time the Jinchuan chieftain Langka and nine chieftains including Choosjab were provoking trouble; A Gui inspected the border, fully learned Langka's cunning and entrenched wickedness, and came to know the terrain and topography, which he reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The Jinchuan chieftain Langka and nine neighboring chieftains including Choosjab were then stirring up trouble; A Gui toured the frontier, documented Langka's deceit and defiance in full, mapped the terrain, and reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 是冬，召還京。

translations.literal: That winter he was recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was recalled to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 三十年，上南巡，命留京治事。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, when the emperor made a southern tour, A Gui was ordered to remain in the capital to handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, while the emperor toured the south, he was left in Beijing to manage state affairs.

sentences.zh: 烏什回賴黑木圖拉作亂，詔馳赴烏什與將軍明瑞攻之，賴黑木圖拉中矢死，眾伯克復推額色木圖拉抗我師，自三月至八月，攻城不下。

translations.literal: The Muslim subject Lai Heimutula of Ush rebelled; an edict ordered A Gui to hurry to Ush and attack with General Mingrui; Lai Heimutula was struck by an arrow and died, but the begs again set up Esemutula to resist our army; from the third month to the eighth month the city could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ush Muslim leader Lai Heimutula rose in revolt, an edict sent A Gui posthaste to join General Mingrui; Lai Heimutula fell to an arrow, but the begs then rallied behind Esemutula to resist the Qing forces, and from the third month through the eighth month the siege would not break.

sentences.zh: 明瑞軍其北，阿桂軍其南，作長圍困之，絕其水道。

translations.literal: Mingrui encamped on the north and A Gui on the south, forming a long encirclement to besiege the city and cut off its water routes.
translations.idiomatic: Mingrui took the north and A Gui the south, tightening a long encirclement around the city and cutting off its water supply.

sentences.zh: 賊糧盡，內訌，沙布勒者擒額色木圖拉以獻，烏什平。

translations.literal: When the rebels' provisions were exhausted, internal strife broke out; Shabulezhe captured Esemutula and presented him, and Ush was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: With their stores exhausted and faction fighting within the walls, Shabulezhe seized Esemutula and handed him over, and Ush was pacified.

sentences.zh: 上責其遲延，示怯損威，部議奪官，命留任，駐雅爾城。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked them for delay, saying it showed cowardice and damaged prestige; the ministry proposed stripping them of office, but the emperor ordered them to remain in post and garrison Yarkand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor blamed them for the delay, saying it had shown weakness and cost imperial prestige; although the ministry recommended dismissal, he kept them in office and stationed A Gui at Yarkand.

sentences.zh: 旋复奪尚書，命還伊犁助明瑞治事。

translations.literal: Soon his ministerial title was again stripped, and he was ordered back to Yili to assist Mingrui in governing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon stripped of his ministerial rank again and sent back to Yili to assist Mingrui in administration.

sentences.zh: 阿桂疏請移雅爾城於楚呼楚，從之。

translations.literal: A Gui memorialized to move Yarkand to Chuchu, and the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: A Gui proposed relocating the Yarkand garrison to Chuchu, and the court approved.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，授伊犁將軍。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he was appointed general of Yili.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year he was appointed general of Yili.

sentences.zh: 請自楚呼楚至烏爾圖布拉克設三台，以通雅爾，下部行。

translations.literal: He requested that three courier stations be set up from Chuchu to Urtubulak to link with Yarkand; the matter was referred to the relevant ministry for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that three courier stations be established from Chuchu to Urtubulak to open communications with Yarkand, and the ministries were ordered to carry this out.

sentences.zh: 緬甸擾邊，總督劉藻、楊應琚先後得罪去，上命明瑞率師討之，至猛育，糧盡，戰沒。

translations.literal: Burma harassed the border; the governors-general Liu Zao and Yang Yingju were successively punished and removed; the emperor ordered Mingrui to lead an army against Burma; reaching Mengyu, provisions ran out and he died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Burma raided the frontier, Governors-General Liu Zao and Yang Yingju were dismissed in turn; the emperor sent Mingrui to lead a punitive expedition, but at Mengyu his supplies gave out and he was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 大學士傅恆自請行，三十三年，以傅恆為經略，阿桂及阿里袞為副將軍，仍授阿桂兵部尚書、雲貴總督。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Fu Heng volunteered to go; in the thirty-third year Fu Heng was made commander-in-chief, and A Gui and Aligun were made deputy commanders; A Gui was again given the posts of Minister of War and governor-general of Yunnan-Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Fu Heng offered to take the field himself; in the thirty-third year he was made commander-in-chief, with A Gui and Aligun as his deputies, while A Gui was again appointed Minister of War and governor-general of Yunnan-Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，以明德為總督，令阿桂專治軍事。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year Mingde was made governor-general and A Gui was ordered to devote himself solely to military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year Mingde became governor-general, leaving A Gui to handle military affairs alone.

sentences.zh: 阿桂請由銅壁關抵蠻暮，伐木造舟，俟經略至軍，進攻老官屯，且言軍糧不給。

translations.literal: A Gui requested to go from Tongbi Pass to Manmu, fell timber to build boats, wait until the commander-in-chief reached the army, then advance against Laoguantun, and also said army provisions were insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: A Gui proposed advancing from Tongbi Pass to Manmu, felling timber to build boats, and attacking Laoguantun once the commander-in-chief arrived, while warning that army rations were inadequate.

sentences.zh: 上以為畏怯，罷副將軍，改授參贊大臣。

translations.literal: The emperor regarded this as timidity, removed him as deputy commander, and reappointed him assisting commander.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took this as cowardice, stripped him of the deputy command, and made him assisting commander instead.

sentences.zh: 九月，舟成，傅恆亦至，分三路進：傅恆出萬仞關，由大金沙江西經猛拱、暮魯至老官屯；

translations.literal: In the ninth month the boats were finished and Fu Heng also arrived; they advanced in three columns: Fu Heng went out from Wanren Pass, along the west bank of the Great Jinsha River through Menggong and Mulu to Laoguantun;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the fleet was ready and Fu Heng reached the front; the army advanced in three columns: Fu Heng marched from Wanren Pass along the west bank of the upper Irrawaddy through Menggong and Mulu toward Laoguantun;

sentences.zh: 阿里袞率舟師循江下；

translations.literal: Aligun led the fleet down the river;
translations.idiomatic: Aligun led the river fleet downstream;

sentences.zh: 阿桂率蠻暮新舟出江會之，先伏兵甘立寨。

translations.literal: A Gui led the new boats from Manmu out onto the river to join them, first placing ambush troops at Ganli Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: A Gui brought the new boats built at Manmu onto the river to rendezvous with them, having first posted ambush troops at Ganli Stockade.

sentences.zh: 緬人從猛戛來拒，寨兵出擊，沉三舟，舟師噪應之，緬人大潰，殲其渠，遂與西岸軍合。

translations.literal: The Burmese came from Mengga to resist; the stockade troops sallied forth, sank three boats, the fleet shouted in response, the Burmese were utterly routed, their leaders were destroyed, and they then joined the army on the west bank.
translations.idiomatic: When the Burmese advanced from Mengga to block them, the ambush force struck, sinking three boats; the fleet roared in support, the Burmese broke completely, their leaders were wiped out, and the columns united on the west bank.

sentences.zh: 老官屯守禦堅，軍士多病瘴，阿里袞卒於軍，复授阿桂副將軍。

translations.literal: Laoguantun was stoutly defended; many soldiers fell ill with miasma; Aligun died in the army, and A Gui was again appointed deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: Laoguantun held firm, malaria swept the ranks, Aligun died in camp, and A Gui was again made deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 傅恆亦病，上命班師，而緬酋懵駁亦懲甘立寨之敗，遣使議受約束，乃召傅恆還。

translations.literal: Fu Heng also fell ill; the emperor ordered withdrawal, but the Burmese chief Meng Bo, chastened by the defeat at Ganli Stockade, sent envoys to discuss accepting restraint, and Fu Heng was then recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng fell ill as well; the emperor ordered a withdrawal, but the Burmese ruler Meng Bo, sobered by the defeat at Ganli Stockade, sent envoys to negotiate submission, and Fu Heng was recalled.

sentences.zh: 命阿桂留辦善後，授禮部尚書。

translations.literal: A Gui was ordered to remain and handle aftermath affairs, and was appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: A Gui was left behind to manage the aftermath and appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，兼鑲紅旗漢軍都統。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year he was additionally appointed commander-in-chief of the Bordered Red Banner Chinese forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year he was also made commander-in-chief of the Bordered Red Banner Chinese forces.

sentences.zh: 命赴騰越待緬人入貢。

translations.literal: He was ordered to go to Tengyue to await the Burmese coming to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to Tengyue to receive the Burmese tribute embassy.

sentences.zh: 遣都司蘇爾相賚檄至老官屯，緬人拘之，索還木邦等三土司。

translations.literal: He sent Colonel Su Erxiang with a dispatch to Laoguantun; the Burmese detained him and demanded the return of the three chieftaincies including Mubang.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Colonel Su Erxiang with an imperial message to Laoguantun; the Burmese seized him and demanded the restoration of Mubang and two other former tributary domains.

sentences.zh: 疏入，上命罷尚書、都統，以內大臣留辦副將軍事。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, the emperor ordered him stripped of the ministerial and commandership posts and left him as inner court minister to handle deputy commander affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When his report reached court, the emperor removed him as minister and banner commander but kept him on as inner court minister to continue deputy command duties.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，疏請大舉徵緬，入覲陳機密。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he memorialized requesting a major campaign against Burma and came to audience to present confidential plans.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year he urged a full-scale campaign against Burma and came to court in person to lay out his confidential strategy.

sentences.zh: 上手詔詰責，命奪官留軍效力。

translations.literal: The emperor personally issued an edict rebuking him and ordered his office stripped while he remained with the army to redeem himself through service.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him in a personal edict, stripped him of rank, and ordered him to remain with the army and earn his way back through service.

sentences.zh: 是時金川酋郎卡已死，其子索諾木及小金川酋澤旺子僧格桑擾邊，四川總督阿爾泰徵之無功，上命阿桂隨副將軍、尚書溫福進討。

translations.literal: At that time the Jinchuan chieftain Langka was already dead; his son Sonom and the Lesser Jinchuan chieftain Zewang's son Senggesang were harassing the border; Sichuan governor-general Ertai campaigned against them without success, and the emperor ordered A Gui to follow Deputy Commander and Minister Wenfu in the advance.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Jinchuan chieftain Langka was dead, but his son Sonom and Zewang's son Senggesang of Lesser Jinchuan were raiding the frontier; Governor-General Ertai's campaign had failed, and the emperor ordered A Gui to join Deputy Commander Wenfu in the advance.

sentences.zh: 十二月，署四川提督，克巴朗拉、達木巴宗各寨。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he acted as Sichuan provincial military commander and captured the stockades of Balangla and Damubazong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, acting as provincial military commander of Sichuan, he took the stockades at Balangla and Damubazong.

sentences.zh: 三十七年二月，克資哩山，進克阿喀木雅。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirty-seventh year he captured Zili Mountain and then advanced to take Akemuya.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the thirty-seventh year he seized Zili Mountain and pressed on to capture Akemuya.

sentences.zh: 松潘總兵宋元俊亦復革布什咱。

translations.literal: Songpan regional commander Song Yuanjun also recovered Gebushizan.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yuanjun, regional commander of Songpan, also recovered Gebushizan.

sentences.zh: 兩金川勢日蹙，合謀抗我師。

translations.literal: The two Jinchuan powers grew daily more pressed and joined in plotting to resist our army.
translations.idiomatic: With both Jinchuan domains growing desperate, they joined forces to resist the Qing armies.

sentences.zh: 上命溫福等三路進討，阿桂出西路阿喀木雅攻喇卜楚克，克之，奪普爾瑪寨，進逼美美卡。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Wenfu and others to advance in three columns; A Gui went out on the western route from Akemuya to attack Labchuk, captured it, seized the Puerma stockade, and pressed toward Meimeika.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered a three-pronged advance under Wenfu; A Gui took the western route from Akemuya against Labchuk, captured it, seized Puerma Stockade, and closed on Meimeika.

sentences.zh: 澤旺為子謝罪，索諾木亦代僧格桑請還侵地，上不許。

translations.literal: Zewang apologized on his son's behalf, and Sonom also pleaded on Senggesang's behalf to return seized lands; the emperor would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Zewang apologized for his son, and Sonom likewise asked on Senggesang's behalf to return occupied territory; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 時侍郎桂林代阿爾泰為總督，並領其眾，至墨隴溝，失利，副將薛琮死之，阿爾泰劾罷桂林。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Minister Guilin replaced Ertai as governor-general and also took over his forces; reaching Molong Ravine, he met defeat and Vice Commander Xue Cong was killed; Ertai impeached and had Guilin dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Guilin had replaced Ertai as governor-general and led his troops to Molong Ravine, where they were beaten and Vice Commander Xue Cong was killed; Ertai impeached Guilin and had him removed.

sentences.zh: 上授阿桂參贊大臣，命赴南路接剿。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed A Gui assisting commander and ordered him to the southern route to take over the pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made him assisting commander and sent him to the southern front to take over the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 僧格宗者，小金川門戶也。

translations.literal: Sengge Stockade was the gateway to Lesser Jinchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sengge Stockade was the gateway to Lesser Jinchuan.

sentences.zh: 甲爾木山梁為僧格宗要徑。

translations.literal: The Jiaermu mountain ridge was the key route to Sengge Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiaermu ridge was the critical approach to Sengge Stockade.

sentences.zh: 阿桂乘賊怠，潛赴墨​​隴溝，夜半大霧，襲據之，進逼僧格宗，突入毀其碉，殲賊無算。

translations.literal: A Gui took advantage of the rebels' negligence, secretly went to Molong Ravine, and in the deep night amid heavy fog seized it by surprise; he pressed on toward Sengge Stockade, burst in and destroyed its blockhouses, and destroyed countless rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Taking advantage of rebel complacency, A Gui stole to Molong Ravine and, in a midnight fog, seized it by surprise; he then pressed on Sengge Stockade, stormed in, smashed its blockhouses, and killed rebels beyond count.

sentences.zh: 上授溫福定邊將軍，豐升額、阿桂俱授副將軍，分道取美諾。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Wenfu Pacification General of the Border, and both Fengsheng'e and A Gui were made deputy commanders to take Meinuo by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: Wenfu was made Pacification General of the Border, with Fengsheng'e and A Gui as his deputies, each marching by a different route to take Meinuo.

sentences.zh: 阿桂克美都喇嘛寺，俯瞰美諾。

translations.literal: A Gui captured the Meidu Lama temple and looked down upon Meinuo.
translations.idiomatic: A Gui captured the Meidu Lama temple, commanding a view over Meinuo below.

sentences.zh: 僧格桑遁布朗郭宗，而溫福亦克西路來會，進剿布朗郭宗。

translations.literal: Senggesang fled to Bulangguo Stockade; Wenfu also captured the western route and came to join him, advancing against Bulangguo Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Senggesang fled to Bulangguo Stockade; Wenfu, having cleared the western route, joined him and they advanced together on Bulangguo Stockade.

sentences.zh: 僧格桑送孥金川而遁底木達，求見父澤旺，澤旺不納，渡河走金川。

translations.literal: Senggesang sent his wife and children to Jinchuan and fled to Dimuda, seeking to see his father Zewang; Zewang would not receive him, and he crossed the river and fled to Jinchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Senggesang sent his family ahead into Jinchuan and fled to Dimuda to see his father Zewang, who refused him; he then crossed the river and fled into Greater Jinchuan.

sentences.zh: 澤旺降，械送京師，小金川平。

translations.literal: Zewang submitted, was sent in fetters to the capital, and Lesser Jinchuan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Zewang surrendered, was sent to Beijing in chains, and Lesser Jinchuan was pacified.

sentences.zh: 於是議討金川，金川賊巢二：曰噶拉依，曰勒烏圍。

translations.literal: Thereupon they deliberated attacking Jinchuan; the rebel strongholds of Jinchuan were two: called Galaiyi and Lewuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Plans were then laid to attack Greater Jinchuan, whose rebel strongholds were Galaiyi and Lewuwei.

sentences.zh: 溫福由功噶爾拉，阿桂由當噶爾拉，合攻噶拉依；

translations.literal: Wenfu went by Gongga'erla and A Gui by Dangga'erla to join in attacking Galaiyi;
translations.idiomatic: Wenfu advanced by Gongga'erla and A Gui by Dangga'erla to combine against Galaiyi;

sentences.zh: 豐升額由綽斯甲布徑攻勒烏圍。

translations.literal: Fengsheng'e advanced directly from Choosjab to attack Lewuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Fengsheng'e took the Choosjab route straight against Lewuwei.

sentences.zh: 复授禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 三十八年正月朔，冒大雪，進奪當功噶爾拉諸碉，而溫福至木果木，索諾木誘降番叛襲軍後，斷登春糧道，我師潰，溫福死之。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of the thirty-eighth year, braving heavy snow, he advanced and seized the blockhouses at Danggongga'erla and elsewhere; meanwhile Wenfu had reached Muguomu, where Sonom induced surrendered tribes to revolt and attack the army from the rear, cut off the Dengchun grain route, our forces were routed, and Wenfu died.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of the thirty-eighth year, the army pushed through heavy snow and captured the Danggongga'erla forts. Meanwhile Wenfu had reached Muguomu; Sonom persuaded the surrendered tribes to rise and strike from the rear, severing the Dengchun supply line. Our forces collapsed, and Wenfu was killed.

sentences.zh: 小金川與美諾等相繼陷。

translations.literal: Lesser Jinchuan, Meinuo, and other places fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser Jinchuan, Meinuo, and other strongholds fell one after another.

sentences.zh: 阿桂悉收降番械，毀碉寨，分置其人章谷、打箭爐，斬其桀驁者，親殿軍退駐達河。

translations.literal: A Gui collected weapons from all the surrendered tribes, destroyed their fortresses and stockades, resettled the people at Zhanggu and Dajianlu, executed the most defiant among them, and personally commanded the rearguard as the army withdrew to encamp at the Da River.
translations.idiomatic: A Gui disarmed the surrendered tribes, demolished their forts and stockades, and resettled the people at Zhanggu and Dajianlu; he executed the most unruly among them, then personally brought up the rear as the army withdrew to the Da River.

sentences.zh: 事聞，上怒甚，命發健銳、火器兩營，黑龍江、吉林、伊犁額魯特兵五千，授阿桂定西將軍，明亮、豐升額副將軍，舒常參贊大臣，整師再出。

translations.literal: When word reached the throne, the emperor was greatly angered. He ordered the Jianrui and Firearms camps and five thousand Oirat troops from Heilongjiang, Jilin, and Yili; he appointed A Gui Pacification General of the West, with Mingliang and Fengsheng'e as deputy commanders and Shuchang as assisting commander, to reorganize the army and march out again.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of this, he was furious. He sent the Jianrui and Firearms camps and five thousand Oirat troops from Heilongjiang, Jilin, and Yili, made A Gui Pacification General of the West with Mingliang and Fengsheng'e as deputies and Shuchang as assisting commander, and ordered the army out again under a fresh command.

sentences.zh: 十月，攻下資哩。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Zili was captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month they captured Zili.

sentences.zh: 用番人木塔爾策，分師由中、南兩路進，潛軍登北山巔，遂取美諾，明亮等亦克僧格宗來會，凡七日，小金川平。

translations.literal: Using the tribal guide Mutar, they divided the army and advanced by central and southern routes; secretly sending troops to the summit of the northern mountain, they then took Meinuo. Mingliang and others also captured Sengge Stockade and joined them. In seven days altogether, Lesser Jinchuan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Following the tribal guide Mutar, they split the force along central and southern routes while secretly posting men on the northern ridge, then seized Meinuo. Mingliang's column also took Sengge Stockade and linked up. Within seven days, Lesser Jinchuan was subdued.

sentences.zh: 三十九年正月朔，阿桂抵布朗郭宗，人裹十日糧，分三隊進，轉戰以前，克喇穆左右二山，贊巴拉克山、色依谷山。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of the thirty-ninth year, A Gui reached Bulangguo Stockade. Each man carried ten days' rations; dividing into three columns, they fought forward and captured the two mountains flanking Lamu, Zhabalake Mountain, and Seyigu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of the thirty-ninth year, A Gui reached Bulangguo Stockade. Each soldier carried ten days' rations; advancing in three columns and fighting as they went, they took the two mountains on either side of Lamu, along with Zhabalake Mountain and Seyigu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 二月，克羅博瓦山，勒烏圍門戶也。

translations.literal: In the second month, they captured Luobowa Mountain—the gateway to Lewuwei.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month they captured Luobowa Mountain, the gateway to Lewuwei.

sentences.zh: 賊退守喇穆山。

translations.literal: The rebels withdrew to hold Lamu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fell back to defend Lamu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 部將海蘭察從間道破色漰普寨，繞出山後，賊退守薩甲山嶺。

translations.literal: The subordinate general Hailancha broke through Seyongpu Stockade by a hidden path and came out behind the mountain; the rebels withdrew to hold the Sa'jia Mountain ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate general Hailancha took Seyongpu Stockade by a hidden route and swung around behind the mountain; the rebels fell back to the Sa'jia Mountain ridge.

sentences.zh: 海蘭察奪其峭壁大碉，諸寨奪氣，同時下，乘勝臨遜克爾宗。

translations.literal: Hailancha seized their great fortress on the cliff; the other stockades lost heart and fell at the same time. Pressing the advantage, they advanced on Xunke'erzong.
translations.idiomatic: Hailancha stormed their cliff-top fortress; the other stockades lost heart and surrendered together. Riding the momentum, the army pressed on to Xunke'erzong.

sentences.zh: 僧格桑死於金川，金川酋獻其屍，而死守遜克爾宗。

translations.literal: Senggesang had died in Jinchuan; the Jinchuan chieftain presented his corpse, yet still held Xunke'erzong to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Senggesang had died in Jinchuan, and the Jinchuan chieftain delivered up his body, but the defenders still held Xunke'erzong to the last.

sentences.zh: 十月，阿桂用策先克默格爾山及凱立葉，於是日爾巴當噶諸碉反在我師後，遂悉平之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, A Gui used a stratagem to capture Mogeer Mountain and Kailiye first; thereupon the forts at Ri'erdangga and elsewhere, which had been behind our army, were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month A Gui first took Mogeer Mountain and Kailiye by stratagem; the forts at Ri'erdangga and elsewhere, which now lay behind our lines, were then cleared one by one.

sentences.zh: 賊退守康薩爾山。

translations.literal: The rebels withdrew to hold Kangsa'er Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fell back to defend Kangsa'er Mountain.

sentences.zh: 時豐升額出北路，師至凱立葉，望見煙火，以師來會；

translations.literal: At this time Fengsheng'e was advancing from the northern route; when his army reached Kailiye and saw signal fires, he knew the main force had come to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Fengsheng'e was moving along the northern route; when his column reached Kailiye and saw the beacon fires, he knew the main army was coming to link up.

sentences.zh: 而明亮出南路，阻於庚額山；

translations.literal: Mingliang, advancing from the southern route, was blocked at Geng'e Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Mingliang, coming up from the south, was held up at Geng'e Mountain.

sentences.zh: 阿桂令移軍，冒雨破宜喜，與明亮軍隔河相望。

translations.literal: A Gui ordered the army to shift position, broke through Yixi in the rain, and faced Mingliang's army across the river.
translations.idiomatic: A Gui shifted his forces, broke through Yixi in the rain, and took up a position facing Mingliang's army across the river.

sentences.zh: 十一月，克格魯克古丫口，金川東北之賊殆盡。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, they captured Gelukeguyakou; the rebels in northeastern Jinchuan were nearly wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month they took Gelukeguyakou, and the rebel forces in northeastern Jinchuan were all but destroyed.

sentences.zh: 四十年正月，克康薩爾山梁。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fortieth year, they captured the Kangsa'er Mountain ridge.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fortieth year they captured the Kangsa'er Mountain ridge.

sentences.zh: 二月，克沿河斯莫思达寨。

translations.literal: In the second month, they captured the Simosi Stockade along the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month they captured the Simosi stockade on the riverbank.

sentences.zh: 四月，克木思工噶克丫口。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, they captured the Musigongakeyakou pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month they took the Musigongakeyakou pass.

sentences.zh: 五月，克下巴木通及勒吉爾博山梁，進據得式梯，复克噶爾丹寺、噶明噶等寨。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, they captured Xiabamutong and the Leji'erbo mountain ridge, advanced to hold Deshiti, and again captured Gama'erdan Monastery, Gamin'ga, and other stockades.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month they took Xiabamutong and the Leji'erbo ridge, pushed forward to Deshiti, and also captured Gama'erdan Monastery, Gamin'ga, and other stockades.

sentences.zh: 進攻巴佔，屢攻不下。

translations.literal: They pressed the attack on Bazhan but repeatedly failed to take it.
translations.idiomatic: They assaulted Bazhan again and again but could not bring it down.

sentences.zh: 分兵從舍圖枉卡繞擊，牽賊勢。

translations.literal: They divided their forces to strike from Shetuwangka by a detour and draw off the enemy's strength.
translations.idiomatic: They split the force to outflank through Shetuwangka and pull the enemy in two directions.

sentences.zh: 七月，克昆色爾及果克多山，進克拉栝寺、菑則大海山梁，旋克章噶。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, they captured Kunse'er and Guokeduo Mountain, advanced to the Kaluo Monastery and Zhai Ze Daha mountain ridges, and soon after took Zhangga.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month they took Kunse'er and Guokeduo Mountain, advanced on Kaluo Monastery and the Zhai Ze Daha ridge, and shortly afterward captured Zhangga.

sentences.zh: 八月，克隆斯得寨，遂克勒烏圍。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, they captured Longside Stockade and then took Lewuwei.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month they captured Longside Stockade and then took Lewuwei.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，上遣阿桂子阿必達齎紅寶石頂賜之。

translations.literal: When word of the victory reached the throne, the emperor sent A Gui's son Abida to present him with a ruby finial as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: When news of the victory arrived, the emperor sent A Gui's son Abida to confer on him a ruby finial.

sentences.zh: 九月，克當噶克底諸寨。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, they captured the stockades at Danggakdi and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month they captured Danggakdi and the surrounding stockades.

sentences.zh: 十月，克達木噶。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, they captured Damuga.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month they captured Damuga.

sentences.zh: 十一月，克西里山雅瑪朋寨。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, they captured the Yamapeng Stockade on Xili Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month they took the Yamapeng stockade on Xili Mountain.

sentences.zh: 十二月，克薩爾歪諸寨，進據噶佔。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, they captured the stockades at Sa'erwai and elsewhere and advanced to hold Gachan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month they captured Sa'erwai and the other stockades and pushed forward to hold Gachan.

sentences.zh: 四十一年正月，克瑪爾古當噶碉寨五百餘，遂圍噶拉依。

translations.literal: In the first month of the forty-first year, they captured more than five hundred fortresses and stockades at Ma'ergudangga and then invested Galaiyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the forty-first year they overran more than five hundred forts and stockades at Ma'ergudangga and then besieged Galaiyi.

sentences.zh: 索諾木母先赴河西集餘眾，大兵合圍，與其子絕，遂降。

translations.literal: Sonom's mother had gone ahead to the west of the river to gather the remaining forces. When the main army closed the encirclement, she was cut off from her son and then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Sonom's mother had crossed to the west of the river to rally the remnants; once the main force completed the encirclement and severed her from her son, she surrendered.

sentences.zh: 阿桂令作書招索諾木，而其頭目降者相繼，索諾木乃率眾降。

translations.literal: A Gui had letters written to summon Sonom; as his subordinate chiefs surrendered one after another, Sonom then led his followers in submission.
translations.idiomatic: A Gui sent written summons to Sonom; as his headmen surrendered in succession, Sonom at last came in with his followers.

sentences.zh: 金川平，安置降番，設副將、同知分駐其地。

translations.literal: Jinchuan was pacified. The surrendered tribes were resettled, and deputy generals and subprefects were posted to garrison the region.
translations.idiomatic: With Jinchuan pacified, the surrendered tribes were resettled and deputy generals and subprefects were stationed across the territory.

sentences.zh: 詔封一等誠謀英勇公，進協辦大學士、吏部尚書、軍機處行走。

translations.literal: An edict enfeoffed him as duke of the first rank with the style Chengmou Yingyong, and promoted him to associate grand secretary, Minister of Personnel, and member of the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: An edict enfeoffed him as first-rank Duke Chengmou Yingyong, promoted him to associate grand secretary and Minister of Personnel, and appointed him to the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 四月，班師。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, the army returned in triumph.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the army marched home in triumph.

sentences.zh: 上幸良鄉城南行郊勞禮，賜御用鞍馬。

translations.literal: The emperor went to the southern outskirts of Liangxiang to perform the suburban ceremony of congratulation and bestowed an imperial saddle and horse.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went to the southern outskirts of Liangxiang to perform the victory ceremony and granted him an imperial saddle and horse.

sentences.zh: 還京獻俘，禦紫光閣，行飲至禮，賜紫韁、四開褉袍。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, he presented captives; at the Hall of Purple Splendor the emperor held the feast of triumph and granted him a purple-bridled horse and a four-panel ceremonial robe.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital he presented the captives; at the Hall of Purple Splendor the emperor held the feast of triumph and bestowed on him a purple-bridled horse and a four-panel ceremonial robe.

sentences.zh: 初，阿桂去雲南，緬甸遣使議入貢，械送京師下獄。

translations.literal: Earlier, when A Gui had left Yunnan, Burma had sent envoys to discuss submitting tribute; they were sent in chains to the capital and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when A Gui had left Yunnan, Burma had sent envoys to discuss paying tribute; they were shackled and sent to the capital for imprisonment.

sentences.zh: 至是誅索諾木母子頭人，上命釋緬使令觀，譯告以故，縱之歸，冀以威武風動之。

translations.literal: At this time, after Sonom, his mother, and the tribal chiefs were executed, the emperor ordered the Burmese envoys released to witness it; an interpreter explained the reason, and they were sent home, in the hope that imperial might would awe them.
translations.idiomatic: Now, after Sonom, his mother, and the tribal chiefs were put to death, the emperor ordered the Burmese envoys released to watch; an interpreter explained why, and they were sent home in the hope that imperial might would strike them with fear.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，署雲貴總督圖思德奏：「懵駁已死，子贅角牙立，輸誠納貢，原歸中國人。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, the acting Yunnan-Guizhou governor Tusi De memorialized: "Meng Bo is dead; his son Zhuajiaoya has succeeded, offers loyalty and tribute, and wishes to return to Chinese rule.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year the acting Yunnan-Guizhou governor Tusi De memorialized: "Meng Bo is dead; his son Zhuajiaoya has succeeded, professes loyalty, offers tribute, and wishes to return to Chinese rule.

sentences.zh: 請開關通市。」

translations.literal: He requests that the border be opened for trade."
translations.idiomatic: He asks that the border be opened for trade."

sentences.zh: 上以事重，當有重臣相度受成，命阿桂往蒞。

translations.literal: The emperor considered the matter weighty and said a senior minister should go to assess and conclude it; he ordered A Gui to proceed and take charge.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged the matter too weighty to be settled lightly and ordered A Gui to go and oversee it in person.

sentences.zh: 五月，授武英殿大學士，管理吏部，兼正紅旗滿洲都統。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory, put in charge of the Ministry of Personnel, and concurrently made commander of the Plain Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory, given charge of the Ministry of Personnel, and concurrently made commander of the Plain Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 緬甸使不至，遣蘇爾相等歸，遂召阿桂還。

translations.literal: The Burmese envoys did not come; Su Erxiang and the others were sent home, and A Gui was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: When the Burmese envoys failed to appear, Su Erxiang and his party were sent home and A Gui was recalled.

sentences.zh: 未幾，緬甸內亂。

translations.literal: Before long, civil strife broke out in Burma.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward civil war erupted in Burma.

sentences.zh: 又十餘年，國王孟隕具表祝上八旬聖壽，定十年一貢。

translations.literal: More than ten years later, King Mengyun submitted a memorial congratulating the emperor on his eightieth birthday and fixed tribute at once every ten years.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten years later King Mengyun sent a memorial congratulating the emperor on his eightieth birthday and agreed to tribute once every ten years.

sentences.zh: 南徼始安。

translations.literal: The southern frontier was at last settled.
translations.idiomatic: The southern frontier was finally at peace.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，河決儀封、蘭陽，奉命往按。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year, the Yellow River broke its banks at Yifeng and Lanyang; he was ordered to go and investigate.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year the Yellow River burst its banks at Yifeng and Lanyang, and he was ordered to go and inspect the breach.

sentences.zh: 阿桂令開郭家莊引河，築攔黃壩；

translations.literal: A Gui ordered the Guojiazhuang diversion channel opened and a blocking dam built to hold back the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: A Gui had the Guojiazhuang diversion channel cut and a blocking dam built against the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 又於下流王家莊，築順黃壩：蓄水勢，逼溜直入引河。

translations.literal: Farther downstream at Wangjiazhuang he also built a guiding dam: storing the force of the water, it drove the current straight into the diversion channel.
translations.idiomatic: Farther downstream at Wangjiazhuang he also built a guiding dam that pooled the water and forced the current directly into the diversion channel.

sentences.zh: 四十五年三月，堤工蕆，還京。

translations.literal: In the third month of the forty-fifth year, the dike works were completed and he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the forty-fifth year the dike works were finished and he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 兼翰林院掌院學士。

translations.literal: He was concurrently appointed Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was also appointed Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 旋命勘浙江海塘，築魚鱗石塘、柴塘，及范公塘。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was ordered to inspect the Zhejiang seawalls and build fish-scale stone dikes, brush dikes, and the Fan Gong Dike.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to inspect the Zhejiang seawalls and build fish-scale stone dikes, brush dikes, and the Fan Gong Dike.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，工成，命順道勘清江陶莊河道高堰石工。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year the works were completed; he was ordered on his way back to inspect the Gaoyan stone works on the Tao Zhuang river channel in Qingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year, once the works were done, he was instructed on his return to inspect the Gaoyan stone works on the Tao Zhuang channel in Qingjiang.

sentences.zh: 甘肅撒拉爾新教蘇四十三與老教仇殺，戕官吏。

translations.literal: In Gansu, Su Forty-three of the New Salar Teaching sect feuded with the Old Teaching and killed officials.
translations.idiomatic: In Gansu, Su Forty-three of the New Salar sect clashed with the Old Teaching and murdered officials.

sentences.zh: 總督勒爾謹捕教首馬明心下獄，同教回民二千餘夜濟洮河犯蘭州，噪索明心。

translations.literal: Governor Le'erjin arrested the sect leader Ma Mingxin and imprisoned him; more than two thousand fellow Muslims crossed the Tao River by night and attacked Lanzhou, clamoring for Mingxin.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Le'erjin arrested the sect leader Ma Mingxin and jailed him; more than two thousand fellow Muslims crossed the Tao River by night, marched on Lanzhou, and demanded Mingxin's release.

sentences.zh: 布政使王廷贊誅明心，賊愈熾。

translations.literal: Financial commissioner Wang Tingzan executed Mingxin; the rebels grew fiercer still.
translations.idiomatic: Financial commissioner Wang Tingzan had Mingxin executed, and the rebellion flared hotter.

sentences.zh: 上命阿桂視師，時阿桂猶在工。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered A Gui to take command of the army; at the time A Gui was still at the construction site.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered A Gui to take field command, though he was still overseeing the construction works.

sentences.zh: 命和珅往督戰，失利。

translations.literal: Heshen was ordered to supervise the campaign and suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Heshen was sent to supervise the campaign and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 賊據龍虎、華林諸山，道險隘。

translations.literal: The rebels held Longhu, Hualin, and other mountains; the passes were steep and narrow.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held Longhu, Hualin, and other mountains where the passes were steep and narrow.

sentences.zh: 阿桂至，設圍絕其水道，進攻之，賊大潰。

translations.literal: When A Gui arrived, he set up a blockade to cut off their water supply and pressed the attack; the rebels were routed in force.
translations.idiomatic: When A Gui arrived he blockaded their water routes and attacked; the rebels broke and fled in disarray.

sentences.zh: 殲蘇四十三，餘黨奔華林寺，焚之​​，無一降者。

translations.literal: Su Forty-three was killed; the remaining followers fled to Hualin Monastery, which was burned down—not one surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Su Forty-three was killed; the survivors retreated to Hualin Monastery, which was burned over them—not one surrendered.

sentences.zh: 甘肅冒賑事發，命按治，盡得大小官吏舞弊分賕狀，讞定，疏請增設倉廒，廣儲糧石，以濟民食。

translations.literal: A scandal over fraudulent famine relief in Gansu broke out; he was ordered to investigate and fully uncovered the bribery and corruption of officials great and small. After the cases were decided, he memorialized requesting additional granaries and expanded grain reserves to relieve the people's hunger.
translations.idiomatic: When a scandal over fraudulent famine relief broke out in Gansu, he was ordered to investigate and fully exposed bribery and corruption among officials high and low. After the verdicts were handed down, he memorialized for new granaries and larger grain reserves to feed the people.

sentences.zh: 秋，河決河南青龍岡，命自甘肅赴河南會河道總督李奉翰督塞河。

translations.literal: In autumn the river broke at Qinglonggang in Henan; he was ordered to leave Gansu for Henan to join River Commissioner Li Fenghan in supervising the closure of the breach.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the river burst at Qinglonggang in Henan; he was ordered to leave Gansu for Henan to join River Commissioner Li Fenghan in closing the breach.

sentences.zh: 故事，河決，當決處兩端築壩，漸近漸合，謂之「合龍」。

translations.literal: By precedent, when a river breaks, dams are built at both ends of the breach and gradually brought together—this is called "closing the dragon."
translations.idiomatic: By custom, when a river breaks its banks, dams are built at both ends of the breach and slowly closed until they meet—this is called "closing the dragon."

sentences.zh: 十二月，兩壩將合，副將李榮吉謂水勢盛，宜緩，阿桂督之急。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, as the two dams were about to meet, Deputy General Li Rongji said the current was too strong and closure should be delayed; A Gui pressed for haste in supervising the work.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, as the two dams were nearly joined, Deputy General Li Rongji argued the current was too fierce and closure should wait; A Gui drove the work forward.

sentences.zh: 既合，屬吏入賀，榮吉獨不至，召之，則對使者曰：「為榮吉謝相公，壩不可恃，不敢離也。」

translations.literal: After the closure, subordinate officials came to congratulate; Li Rongji alone did not appear. When summoned, he told the messenger: "Please thank the minister for Li Rongji—the dam cannot be trusted; I dare not leave it."
translations.idiomatic: Once the closure was complete, his subordinates came to congratulate him, but Li Rongji alone stayed away. When summoned, he told the messenger: "Thank the minister for me—Li Rongji cannot trust this dam and dares not leave his post."

sentences.zh: 越二日，果復決，阿桂馳視。

translations.literal: Two days later the breach indeed reopened; A Gui rode out to inspect it.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later the breach broke open again, and A Gui galloped out to inspect it.

sentences.zh: 榮吉已墮水，懸千金賞救之起，解御賜黑狐端罩覆之。

translations.literal: Li Rongji had already fallen into the water; A Gui offered a thousand taels of silver for his rescue, and when he was pulled out, covered him with an imperial black-fox surcoat.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rongji had already fallen into the water; A Gui posted a reward of a thousand taels for his rescue, and when he was hauled out, draped him in an imperial black-fox surcoat.

sentences.zh: 因上疏自劾，請別簡大臣董其役，上詔答，略曰：「近年諸臣中能勝治河任者，舍阿桂豈復有人？

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted a memorial impeaching himself and asking that another senior minister be chosen to direct the works. The emperor replied in an edict, in brief: "Among the ministers of recent years who can bear the task of river control, apart from A Gui, is there anyone else?
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized impeaching himself and asking that another senior minister be appointed to oversee the works. The emperor replied in an edict that, in essence, said: "Of all the ministers in recent years who can manage the rivers, who besides A Gui is fit for the task?

sentences.zh: 惟當安心靜鎮，別求善策。」

translations.literal: You need only settle your mind and keep calm, and seek another good plan."
translations.idiomatic: You need only keep your composure and find a better plan."

sentences.zh: 四十七年，奏請於下游疏引河，上游築大堤，並於北岸建壩，迫溜南趨。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year he memorialized requesting diversion channels downstream, great dikes upstream, and dams on the north bank to force the current southward.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year he memorialized for diversion channels downstream, major dikes upstream, and dams on the north bank to drive the current south.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，工始竟，詣熱河行在，復命仍赴工次，審定章程。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year the works were at last completed; he went to the emperor's traveling palace at Rehe to report, received new orders, and was again sent to the worksite to finalize the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year the works were finally finished; he went to the imperial camp at Rehe to report, received fresh orders, and was sent back to the site to fix the regulations.

sentences.zh: 浙江布政使盛住疏論總督陳輝祖籍王亶望家有所私，命阿桂如浙江按治。

translations.literal: Zhejiang financial commissioner Sheng Zhu memorialized that Governor Chen Huizu had private ties to the family of Wang Tanwang; the emperor ordered A Gui to go to Zhejiang to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang financial commissioner Sheng Zhu reported that Governor Chen Huizu was privately tied to the family of Wang Tanwang; the emperor ordered A Gui to Zhejiang to investigate.

sentences.zh: 還，又命勘江南鹽河水道，又命勘河南蘭陽十二堡堤工，並於戴村建閘。

translations.literal: On his return he was again ordered to inspect the salt-river waterways in Jiangnan, to inspect the dike works at the Twelve Forts of Lanyang in Henan, and to build a sluice at Daicun.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was again ordered to inspect the salt-river channels in Jiangnan, the dike works at Lanyang's Twelve Forts in Henan, and to build a sluice at Daicun.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，甘肅鹽茶廳回民張阿渾據石峰堡以叛。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year, the Muslim Zhang Ahun of Yancha Department in Gansu seized Shifeng Fort and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year the Muslim Zhang Ahun of Yancha Department in Gansu seized Shifeng Fort and rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 上遣福康安、海蘭察等討之，復命阿桂視師。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched Fuk'anggan, Hailancha, and others to suppress him, and again ordered A Gui to take command.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Fuk'anggan, Hailancha, and others to suppress him and again ordered A Gui to oversee the campaign.

sentences.zh: 兩月餘，破堡，戮張阿渾等，加一等輕車都尉世職。

translations.literal: After a little more than two months the fort was taken; Zhang Ahun and the others were executed, and A Gui was granted the additional hereditary rank of first-class Commandant of Light Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: In little more than two months the fort fell; Zhang Ahun and his followers were executed, and A Gui was granted the additional hereditary rank of first-class Commandant of Light Chariots.

sentences.zh: 又命督河南睢州堤工。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to supervise the dike works at Suizhou in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was again ordered to supervise the Suizhou dikes in Henan.

sentences.zh: 五十年，舉千叟宴，阿桂領班。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year, at the banquet for a thousand elders, A Gui led the assembly.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth year, at the Feast of a Thousand Elders, A Gui led the assembly.

sentences.zh: 又命勘河南睢州河工，並察洪澤湖、清口形勢。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to inspect the Suizhou river works in Henan and to survey the conditions at Hongze Lake and Qingkou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again ordered to inspect the Suizhou river works in Henan and survey Hongze Lake and Qingkou.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，又命勘清口堤工，並如浙江按倉庫虧缺，勘海塘；

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year he was again ordered to inspect the Qingkou dikes, to go to Zhejiang to investigate granary shortfalls, and to inspect the seawalls.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year he was again ordered to inspect the Qingkou dikes, investigate granary shortfalls in Zhejiang, and inspect the seawalls.

sentences.zh: 又命勘江南桃源、安東河決。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to inspect the river breaches at Taoyuan and Andong in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered to inspect the river breaches at Taoyuan and Andong in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 再如浙江按治平陽知縣黃梅重徵，論如律。

translations.literal: He went again to Zhejiang to investigate Pingyang magistrate Huang Mei for excessive taxation; the case was decided according to law.
translations.idiomatic: He went again to Zhejiang to investigate Pingyang magistrate Huang Mei for excessive levies; the verdict followed the law.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，又命督塞睢州十三堡河決。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year he was again ordered to supervise the closure of the river breach at the Thirteen Forts of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-second year he was again ordered to supervise closing the breach at Suizhou's Thirteen Forts.

sentences.zh: 時台灣民林爽文叛，上命福康安討之，諮阿桂軍事。

translations.literal: At this time the Taiwan commoner Lin Shuangwen rebelled; the emperor ordered Fuk'anggan to suppress him and consulted A Gui on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Taiwan commoner Lin Shuangwen rebelled; the emperor ordered Fuk'anggan to suppress him and consulted A Gui on strategy.

sentences.zh: 阿桂疏論師當扼要害，分道並進，先通諸羅道，廓清後路，自大甲溪進兵。

translations.literal: A Gui memorialized that the army should seize the key points, advance on separate routes at once, first open the road to Zhuluo, clear the rear, and then march from the Dajia River.
translations.idiomatic: A Gui memorialized that the army should hold the critical points, advance on separate routes at once, first reopen the road to Zhuluo and secure the rear, then push forward from the Dajia River.

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「所見與朕略同，已諭福康安奉方略。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "Your view largely agrees with mine; Fuk'anggan has already been instructed to follow this plan."
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "Your view largely matches my own; Fuk'anggan has already been instructed to follow it."

sentences.zh: 睢州工竟，又命勘江南臨湖磚石堤工。

translations.literal: When the Suizhou works were finished, he was again ordered to inspect the brick-and-stone dikes along the lakes in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Suizhou works were complete, he was again ordered to inspect the lakeside brick-and-stone dikes in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，又命按湖北荊州水災。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year he was again ordered to investigate the flood disaster in Jingzhou, Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-third year he was again ordered to investigate the flooding in Jingzhou, Hubei.

sentences.zh: 請疏窖金洲以導水，修萬城堤以護城。

translations.literal: He requested dredging Jinjizhou to channel the water and repairing the Wancheng Dike to protect the city.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to dredge Jinjizhou to draw off the water and repair the Wancheng Dike to protect the city.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，命再勘荊州堤工。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year he was ordered to inspect the Jingzhou dikes again.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fourth year he was ordered to inspect the Jingzhou dikes again.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，高宗內禪，阿桂奉冊寶。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Jiaqing reign, when the Gaozong Emperor abdicated in favor of his successor, A Gui carried the imperial seals and regalia.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiaqing, when the Gaozong Emperor abdicated, A Gui bore the imperial seals and regalia.

sentences.zh: 再舉千叟宴，仍領班，於是阿桂年八十矣，疏辭領兵部。

translations.literal: At the second Feast of a Thousand Elders he again led the assembly; by then A Gui was eighty years old and memorialized declining the post of Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: At the second Feast of a Thousand Elders he again led the assembly; by then A Gui was eighty and memorialized to resign as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 二年八月，卒，仁宗臨其喪。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year he died; the Renzong Emperor attended his funeral in person.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year he died, and the Renzong Emperor came in person to mourn him.

sentences.zh: 贈太保，祀賢良祠，諡文成。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, enshrined in the Temple of Worthies, and given the posthumous title Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, enshrined in the Temple of Worthies, and given the posthumous title Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 阿桂屢將大軍，知人善任使。

translations.literal: A Gui repeatedly commanded great armies and knew men well, employing them effectively.
translations.idiomatic: Time and again A Gui led major armies, knowing how to recognize talent and put it to use.

sentences.zh: 諸將有戰績，獎以數語，或賚酒食，其人輒感激效死終其身。

translations.literal: When generals achieved merit in battle, he rewarded them with a few words or bestowed wine and food; they would then be moved to gratitude and devote themselves to death for the rest of their lives.
translations.idiomatic: When a general distinguished himself, A Gui might reward him with a brief word of praise or a gift of wine and food; the man would then serve him unto death for the rest of his days.

sentences.zh: 臨敵，夜對酒，深念得策，輒持酒以起，旦必有所號令。

translations.literal: Facing the enemy, he would drink wine at night; when he deeply thought he had found a stratagem, he would rise with his cup in hand, and by morning there would certainly be some order issued.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of battle he would drink deep into the night; when a plan took shape in his mind he would rise with his cup, and by morning there was always a new command.

sentences.zh: 方溫福敗，受命代將。

translations.literal: Just as Wenfu had been defeated, he received orders to replace him as commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenfu's army collapsed, he was ordered to take command in his place.

sentences.zh: 一日日欲暮，率十數騎升高阜覘賊砦。

translations.literal: One day as evening approached, he led a dozen horsemen up a high mound to observe the rebel stockades.
translations.idiomatic: One evening he took a dozen horsemen up a high knoll to scout the rebel fortifications.

sentences.zh: 賊望見，獷騎數百環阜上。

translations.literal: The rebels saw them; several hundred fierce horsemen ringed the mound.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels spotted them, and several hundred mounted warriors surrounded the height.

sentences.zh: 阿桂令從騎皆下馬，解衣裂懸林木，乃令上馬徐下阜。

translations.literal: A Gui ordered his escort all to dismount, stripped off their clothes and hung them on the trees, then ordered them to mount again and descend the mound slowly.
translations.idiomatic: A Gui had his escort dismount, hung their cloaks on the trees to resemble additional troops, remounted, and rode slowly down the slope.

sentences.zh: 賊迫阜，從落日中睹旂幟，疑我師眾，方遣騎出偵，阿桂已還軍矣。

translations.literal: The rebels pressed the mound; in the setting sun they glimpsed banners and flags and suspected a large force; just as they sent riders out to reconnoiter, A Gui had already returned to camp.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels closed on the hill; in the sunset they mistook the hanging garments for banners and feared a large army—by the time their scouts rode out, A Gui was already back in camp.

sentences.zh: 師薄噶拉依，索諾木約以明日降，城柵盡毀。

translations.literal: As the army pressed Galaiyi, Sonom agreed to submit the next day, and the city palisades were all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: As the army closed on Galaiyi, Sonom promised to surrender the next day and had the outer defenses torn down.

sentences.zh: 日暮，諸將謁阿桂，謂：「今日必生致索諾木，不然，慮有他。」

translations.literal: At dusk the generals came to A Gui and said: "Today we must take Sonom alive; otherwise I fear something else may happen."
translations.idiomatic: At dusk his generals urged him: "We must seize Sonom tonight, or he may yet slip away."

sentences.zh: 阿桂不答，入帳臥。

translations.literal: A Gui did not answer and went into his tent to sleep.
translations.idiomatic: A Gui said nothing and retired to his tent to sleep.

sentences.zh: 明旦，索諾木自縛詣帳下。

translations.literal: At dawn Sonom came bound in person to the tent.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Sonom arrived at the tent with his hands bound.

sentences.zh: 阿桂謂諸將曰：「諸君昨日語，蓋慮索諾木他竄，或且死。

translations.literal: A Gui said to the generals: "What you said yesterday was because you feared Sonom might flee elsewhere, or perhaps die.
translations.idiomatic: A Gui told the generals: "Yesterday you worried that Sonom might flee or take his own life.

sentences.zh: 我已得險要，竄安之？

translations.literal: I have already secured the strategic points—where could he flee?
translations.idiomatic: I have already seized the passes—where could he run?

sentences.zh: 且能死，豈至今日？

translations.literal: And if he were willing to die, would he have waited until today?
translations.idiomatic: If he meant to die for his cause, would he have waited until today?

sentences.zh: 故吾以為無慮。」

translations.literal: Therefore I thought there was no cause for concern."
translations.idiomatic: That is why I was not worried."

sentences.zh: 諸將皆謝服。

translations.literal: The generals all thanked him and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The generals bowed in acknowledgment.

sentences.zh: 及執政，尤識​​大體。

translations.literal: After he took power in government, he was especially mindful of the larger pattern.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was especially attentive to the larger interests of state.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，諸行省提鎮以次即有空名坐糧，雍正八年著為例。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi reign, provincial commanders and generals in succession had phantom posts on the rolls; in the eighth year of Yongzheng this was made a formal regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi, provincial commanders and generals had long kept phantom names on the rolls; in the eighth year of Yongzheng this practice was codified.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十七年詔補實額，別給養廉。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year of Qianlong an edict ordered the rolls filled with real numbers and integrity-nurturing allowances given separately.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong's forty-seventh year an edict required real troop numbers on the rolls and separate integrity-nurturing allowances.

sentences.zh: 阿桂疏言：「國家經費驟加不覺其多，歲支則難為繼。

translations.literal: A Gui memorialized: "When state expenditures increase suddenly, one does not notice how large they are; paid out year by year, they become hard to sustain.
translations.idiomatic: A Gui warned: "When spending rises all at once, the total is easy to miss; stretched out year by year, it becomes impossible to maintain.

sentences.zh: 此新增之餉，歲近三百萬，二十餘年即需七千萬。

translations.literal: This newly added pay amounts to nearly three million taels a year; in a little more than twenty years it will require seventy million.
translations.idiomatic: These new salaries come to nearly three million taels a year; in little more than twenty years that will mean seventy million.

sentences.zh: 請除邊省外，無庸概增。」

translations.literal: I request that apart from the border provinces, there is no need to increase them across the board.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that increases be limited to the frontier provinces and not applied everywhere."

sentences.zh: 上不從。

translations.literal: The emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not accept his advice.

sentences.zh: 是時帑藏盈溢，其後漸至虛匱。

translations.literal: At that time the treasury was overflowing; afterward it gradually became depleted.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury was then flush; in time it was gradually drained.

sentences.zh: 此其一端也。

translations.literal: This was one cause of that.
translations.idiomatic: This was one reason why.

sentences.zh: 乾隆末，和珅勢漸張，阿桂遇之不稍假借。

translations.literal: Late in the Qianlong reign, Heshen's power gradually expanded; A Gui never yielded to him in the slightest.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Qianlong's reign, as Heshen's power grew, A Gui never indulged him in the least.

sentences.zh: 不與同直廬，朝夕入直，必離立數十武。

translations.literal: He would not attend duty in the same office; morning and evening when entering duty he always stood several tens of paces apart.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to share a duty room; when they reported for duty morning and evening, he always stood dozens of paces away.

sentences.zh: 和珅就與語，漫應之，終不移一步。

translations.literal: When Heshen came over to speak with him, he answered casually but never moved a single step.
translations.idiomatic: If Heshen came over to talk, he answered briefly and never shifted his footing.

sentences.zh: 阿桂內念位將相，受恩遇無與比，乃坐視其亂政，徒以高宗春秋高，不敢遽言，遂未竟其志。

translations.literal: In his heart A Gui thought that having reached the rank of chief minister and general, with favor unmatched, he yet sat by and watched Heshen's corrupt government; only because the Gaozong Emperor was advanced in years did he not dare speak out at once, and so he did not fulfill his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Privately he knew that, having risen to the highest civil and military rank on unmatched imperial favor, he was watching Heshen's abuses without stopping them; with the emperor aged, he dared not speak out boldly, and so died with his purpose unfulfilled.

sentences.zh: 高宗圖功臣於紫光閣，前後凡四舉，列於前者親為之贊。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor had portraits of meritorious ministers painted in the Hall of Purple Splendor; in all there were four occasions, and for those listed in the foremost rank he personally composed encomia.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaozong Emperor commissioned portraits of meritorious ministers in the Hall of Purple Splendor on four occasions; for those ranked foremost he wrote the laudatory inscriptions himself.

sentences.zh: 定伊犁回部五十人：大學士傅恆，將軍兆惠、班第、納木札爾，副將軍策布登扎布、富德、薩拉爾，大學士總督黃廷桂，參贊大臣親王色布騰巴爾珠爾，貝子扎拉豐阿，郡王羅卜藏多爾濟、額敏和卓，尚書舒赫德、阿里袞，總督鄂容安，侍郎明瑞、阿桂、三泰、鄂實，領隊大臣內大臣博爾奔察，提督豆斌、高天喜，副都統端濟布，護軍統領愛隆阿，前鋒統領瑪巘，副都統巴圖濟爾噶爾，散秩大臣齊凌扎布、噶布舒，郡王霍集斯，貝子鄂對，內大臣鄂齊爾，散秩大臣阿玉錫、達什策淩，副都統鄂博什、溫布、由屯、三格，侍衛奇徹布、老格、達克、塔納、薩穆坦、璊綽爾圖、塔瑪鼐、富錫爾、海蘭察、富紹、扎奇圖、阿爾丹察、五十保。

translations.literal: For the pacification of Yili and the Muslim regions, fifty men: Grand Secretary Fu Heng; Generals Zhao Hui, Ban Di, Namuzha'er; Deputy Generals Tsebudengjab, Fude, Salar; Grand Secretary and Governor-General Huang Tinggui; Assisting Commander and Prince Sebeteng Baljur; Prince Zhalafeng'a; Princes Luobuzang Duo'erji and Emin Hezhuo; Ministers Shuhede and Aligun; Governor-General E Rong'an; Vice Ministers Mingrui, A Gui, Santai, and E Shi; Inner Court Minister and Column Commander Bo'erbengcha; Regional Commanders Dou Bin and Gao Tianxi; Vice Commander-in-Chief Duanjibu; Guard Commander Ailong'a; Vanguard Commander Ma Yan; Vice Commander-in-Chief Batu Ji'erga'er; Ministers without Portfolio Qiling Zhabu, Gabushu, Huo Jisi, E Dui, E Qi'er, Ayu Xi, Dashice Ling, E Boshi, Wenbu, Youtun, Sange, and the guards Qichebu, Laoge, Dake, Tana, Samutan, Man Chuo'ertu, Tamannai, Fuxi'er, Hailancha, Fushao, Zhaqitu, A'erdancha, and Wushibao.
