translations.idiomatic: For the pacification of Yili and the Muslim west, fifty men were honored: Grand Secretary Fu Heng; Generals Zhao Hui, Ban Di, and Namuzha'er; Deputy Generers Tsebudengjab, Fude, and Salar; Grand Secretary and Governor-General Huang Tinggui; Assisting Commander Prince Sebeteng Baljur; Princes Zhalafeng'a, Luobuzang Duo'erji, and Emin Hezhuo; Ministers Shuhede and Aligun; Governor-General E Rong'an; Vice Ministers Mingrui, A Gui, Santai, and E Shi; Inner Court Minister and column commander Bo'erbengcha; regional commanders Dou Bin and Gao Tianxi; vice commanders Duanjibu and Ailong'a; vanguard commander Ma Yan; and the many other officers, princes, guards, and ministers listed in the roster, ending with Wushibao.

sentences.zh: 定金川五十人：將軍阿桂，副將軍豐升額、明亮，大學士舒赫德、於敏中，尚書福隆安，參贊大臣親王色布騰巴爾珠爾，都統海蘭察，護軍統領額森特、舒常，領隊大臣都統奎林、和隆武、福康安，副都統普爾普，荊州將軍興兆，參贊大臣提督哈國興，領隊大臣提督馬彪、馬全、書麟，副都統三保、烏什哈達、瑚尼爾圖、珠爾格德、阿爾都、阿爾薩朗、舒亮、科瑪、伊蘭保、佛倫泰、富興、德赫布、莽喀察，總兵海祿、敖成、官達色​​、成德、欽保、曹順、保寧、特成額、烏爾納，總兵敦柱，侍衛額爾特、托爾托保、泰斐英阿、柏凌、達蘭泰、薩爾吉岱，佐領特爾惇澈，副將興奎。

translations.literal: For the pacification of Jinchuan, fifty men: General A Gui; Deputy Generals Fengsheng'e and Mingliang; Grand Secretaries Shuhede and Yu Minzhong; Minister Fulong'an; Assisting Commander Prince Sebeteng Baljur; Commander-in-Chief Hailancha; Guard Commanders Esente and Shuchang; Column Commanders Kuilin, Helongwu, and Fuk'anggan; Vice Commander-in-Chief Pu'erpu; Jingzhou General Xingzhao; Assisting Commander and Regional Commander Ha Guoxing; Column Commanders and Regional Commanders Ma Biao, Ma Quan, and Shu Lin; Vice Commanders Sanbao, Wushi Hada, Huni'ertu, Zhu'ergede, A'erdu, A'ersalang, Shuliang, Kema, Yilanbao, Foluntai, Fuxing, Dehebu, Mangkacha; Regional Commanders Hailu, Aocheng, Guandase, Chengde, Qinbao, Caoshun, Baoning, Techeng'e, and Wu'erna; Regional Commander Dunzhu; and the guards E'erte, Tuo'ertuobao, Taifeiying'a, Boling, Dalantai, Sa'erjidai, the adjutant Te'erdun Che, and Vice General Xingkui.
translations.idiomatic: For the pacification of Jinchuan, fifty men were honored, headed by General A Gui with Deputy Generals Fengsheng'e and Mingliang, Grand Secretaries Shuhede and Yu Minzhong, Minister Fulong'an, Prince Sebeteng Baljur, Commander-in-Chief Hailancha, Guard Commanders Esente and Shuchang, column commanders Kuilin, Helongwu, and Fuk'anggan, and the full roster of vice commanders, regional commanders, guards, and adjutants ending with Vice General Xingkui.

sentences.zh: 定台灣二十人：大學士阿桂、和珅、王杰，協辦大學士福康安，領侍衛內大臣海蘭察，尚書福長安、董誥，總督李侍堯、孫士毅，巡撫徐嗣曾，成都將軍鄂輝，護軍統領舒亮、普爾普，提督蔡攀龍、梁朝柱、許世亨，總兵穆克登阿、張芝元、普吉保，散秩大臣穆塔爾。

translations.literal: For the pacification of Taiwan, twenty men: Grand Secretaries A Gui, Heshen, and Wang Jie; Associate Grand Secretary Fuk'anggan; Inner Court Minister of the Imperial Guard Hailancha; Ministers Fuchang'an and Dong Gao; Governors-General Li Shiyao and Sun Shiyi; Governor Xu Siceng; Chengdu General E Hui; Guard Commanders Shuliang and Pu'erpu; Regional Commanders Cai Panlong, Liang Chaozhu, and Xu Shiheng; Regional Commanders Mukedeng'a, Zhang Zhiyuan, and Pujibao; Minister without Portfolio Mutar.
translations.idiomatic: For the pacification of Taiwan, twenty men were honored: Grand Secretaries A Gui, Heshen, and Wang Jie; Associate Grand Secretary Fuk'anggan; Inner Court Minister Hailancha; Ministers Fuchang'an and Dong Gao; Governors-General Li Shiyao and Sun Shiyi; Governor Xu Siceng; Chengdu General E Hui; guard commanders Shuliang and Pu'erpu; regional commanders Cai Panlong, Liang Chaozhu, Xu Shiheng, Mukedeng'a, Zhang Zhiyuan, and Pujibao; and Minister without Portfolio Mutar.

sentences.zh: 定廓爾喀十五人：大學士福康安、阿桂、和坤、王杰、孫士毅，領侍衛內大臣海蘭察，尚書福長安、董誥、慶桂、和琳，總督惠齡，護軍統領台斐英阿、額勒登保，副都統阿滿泰、成德。

translations.literal: For the pacification of Gurkha, fifteen men: Grand Secretaries Fuk'anggan, A Gui, Heshen, Wang Jie, and Sun Shiyi; Inner Court Minister Hailancha; Ministers Fuchang'an, Dong Gao, Qing Gui, and Helin; Governor-General Hui Ling; Guard Commanders Taifeiying'a and E'erdengbao; Vice Commanders A'mantai and Chengde.
translations.idiomatic: For the pacification of Gurkha, fifteen men were honored: Grand Secretaries Fuk'anggan, A Gui, Heshen, Wang Jie, and Sun Shiyi; Inner Court Minister Hailancha; Ministers Fuchang'an, Dong Gao, Qing Gui, and Helin; Governor-General Hui Ling; Guard Commanders Taifeiying'a and E'erdengbao; and Vice Commanders A'mantai and Chengde.

sentences.zh: 功稍次者列於後，儒臣為之贊，惟阿桂與海蘭察四次皆前列。

translations.literal: Those of slightly lesser merit were listed afterward, with encomia written by scholar-officials; only A Gui and Hailancha were ranked foremost on all four occasions.
translations.idiomatic: Men of slightly lesser merit were listed behind them, with encomia composed by scholar-officials; only A Gui and Hailancha were placed foremost on all four lists.

sentences.zh: 阿桂定金川元功，定台灣首輔，皆第一；

translations.literal: For Jinchuan, A Gui's was the decisive merit; for Taiwan he was the leading minister—both times he ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinchuan roll his was the decisive merit; in the Taiwan roll he was the leading minister—in both he stood first.

sentences.zh: 定廓爾喀以爵复第一，讓於福康安。

translations.literal: For Gurkha, though by rank he should again have been first, he yielded the place to Fuk'anggan.
translations.idiomatic: For Gurkha he would again have ranked first by merit, but he yielded the place to Fuk'anggan.

sentences.zh: 道光三年二月，宣宗命配饗太廟。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year of Daoguang, the Xuanzong Emperor ordered that he receive paired sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Daoguang's third year, the Xuanzong Emperor ordered him accorded paired sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 子阿迪斯、阿必達。

translations.literal: His sons were Adisi and Abida.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Adisi and Abida.

sentences.zh: 阿迪斯，初以三等侍衛坐阿桂徵緬甸無功，奪職，發遣廣西右江鎮。

translations.literal: Adisi, at first a third-rank guardsman, was stripped of office because A Gui's Burma campaign had achieved no result, and was sent in exile to Youjiang in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Adisi began as a third-rank guardsman but lost his post when his father's Burma campaign failed, and was exiled to Youjiang in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 逾年赦复官。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was pardoned and restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was pardoned and restored to office.

sentences.zh: 累遷兵部侍郎，襲一等公。

translations.literal: He was promoted through several posts to vice minister of War and inherited the dukedom of the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to vice minister of War and inherited the first-rank dukedom.

sentences.zh: 复累遷成都將軍。

translations.literal: He was again promoted through several posts to general of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to general of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 以川西盜發，逮問，發遣伊犁。

translations.literal: Because bandits broke out in western Sichuan, he was arrested for inquiry and sent in exile to Yili.
translations.idiomatic: When banditry erupted in western Sichuan he was arrested, tried, and exiled to Yili.

sentences.zh: 赦歸。

translations.literal: He was pardoned and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He was later pardoned and allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 阿必達，初名阿彌達，高宗命更名。

translations.literal: Abida, originally named Amita, was renamed by order of the Gaozong Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Abida, originally named Amita, was renamed by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 阿桂得罪，奪藍翎侍衛，發遣廣東雷瓊鎮。

translations.literal: When A Gui was punished, Abida was stripped of his blue-lanyard guardsman's post and sent in exile to Leiqiong in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: When A Gui fell from favor, Abida was stripped of his blue-lanyard guardsman's rank and exiled to Leiqiong in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 赦歸，复官。

translations.literal: He was pardoned and returned, and his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: He was pardoned, restored to office, and allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 擢二等侍衛，命赴西寧祭告河神，探黃河真源，上命輯入河源紀略。

translations.literal: He was promoted to second-rank guardsman, ordered to go to Xining to announce sacrifices to the river god and explore the true source of the Yellow River; the emperor ordered his findings compiled into the Records of the River Source.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to second-rank guardsman, he was sent to Xining to announce sacrifices to the river god and trace the true source of the Yellow River; the emperor ordered his report compiled into the Records of the River Source.

sentences.zh: 累遷工部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted through several posts to vice minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 阿必達子那彥寶，官至成都將軍；

translations.literal: Abida's son was Nayenbao, who reached the post of general of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Abida's son Nayenbao rose to general of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 那彥成，自有傳。

translations.literal: Nayancheng has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Nayancheng is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 論曰：將者國之輔，智信仁勇，合群策群力冶而用之，是之謂大將。

translations.literal: Commentary says: The general is the state's support; wisdom, trustworthiness, benevolence, and courage, together with the collective strategies and strengths of many, refined and applied—this is called a great commander.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary observes: A general is the state's pillar. Wisdom, trustworthiness, benevolence, and courage, together with the pooled counsel and strength of many, shaped and deployed as one—this is what makes a great commander.

sentences.zh: 由是道也，佐天子辨章國政，豈有二術哉？

translations.literal: By this path, assisting the Son of Heaven in ordering the nation's government—can there be two methods?
translations.idiomatic: By that same path one assists the Son of Heaven in governing the realm—what second art is there?

sentences.zh: 乾隆間，國軍屢出，熊羆之士，因事而有功；

translations.literal: During the Qianlong reign the national armies went forth repeatedly, and warriors of fierce mettle won merit as occasions arose.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qianlong the armies marched out again and again, and fierce fighters won fame as events demanded.

sentences.zh: 然開誠佈公，謀定而後動，負士民司命之重，固無如阿桂者。

translations.literal: Yet in opening sincerity and spreading fairness, in planning before acting, and in bearing the heavy charge of soldiers and people alike, there was truly none like A Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in candor, in settling plans before acting, and in bearing the lives of soldiers and civilians alike, none matched A Gui.

sentences.zh: 還領樞密，決疑定計，瞻言百里，非同時諸大臣所能及，豈不偉歟？

translations.literal: Returning to head the secretariat, resolving doubts and fixing plans, seeing a hundred li ahead in counsel—this was not something the other great ministers of the time could equal; was it not magnificent?
translations.idiomatic: Back at the helm of the Grand Council, resolving doubts and fixing strategy with foresight far beyond his peers—he stood above the other great ministers of his age. Was that not magnificent?
